newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - UPM streamlines in pulp deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UPM streamlines in pulp deal.

text.p: Europe's largest forestry group, UPM-Kymmene, on Tuesday announced several deals to streamline its structure and bolster its main pulp supplier.
With rival Metsa-Serla Oy, the company said it would channel pulp operations through the Metsa-Botnia pulp mill which the two jointly own, involving a slight boost in capacity.

In operation since May after the merger that created it, UPM said it would sell two mills for a total of about two billion markka ($430 million), in deals yielding a profit of about 700 million markka.
"For us, this solution is a straightforward streamlining of a big company," UPM-Kymmene CEO Juha Niemela told a news conference.
He said the arrangements would strengthen Metsa-Botnia -- in which UPM holds a 47 percent stake -- and ensure the supply of pulp for UPM.
Overall, the firms said the deal would boost their annual pulp capacity by about 30,000 tonnes to around four million tonnes.
Metsa-Serla will buy paperboard, paper and carton mills in Simpele from UPM and Metsa-Botnia will buy UPM's pulp mill in Joutseno, which it will rebuild in a 650 million markka investment.
Also boosting Metsa-Botnia, Metsa-Serla will sell its pulp mill in Aanekoski to the unit.

Metsa-Serla said the deals -- due to be completed in the first quarter of 1997 -- would add about two billion markka to its annual sales of 13.12 billion and make it Europe's second largest producer of folding boxboard.
Its cash outlay in the deals will total 870 million markka.

"We will now reach a good position in Europe," Jorma Vaajoki, Metsa-Serla's chief executive officer, told the news conference, indicating a graph showing Metsa-Serla in second position after Sweden's Stora.
Channelling pulp operations through Metsa-Botnia would dampen the impact of cyclical fluctuations on its financial results, Metsa-Serla added.
Analysts generally welcomed the news, although many found the string of related purchases hard to interpret.
"The transaction looks sensible from UPM-Kymmene's perspective," said Hakan Ostling at Goldman Sachs.
"It represents a step in the direction of increased focus and streamlining, which is the right direction for the pulp and paper industry," he said.
Shares in the companies rose after the news, later trimming gains, with UPM marked up 2.50 markka at 96.50 and Metsa-Serla 0.50 at 34.50.
"For UPM, the deal won't have any real effect on its (longer term) earnings outlook but it's a significant (book) profit," said Jukka Huuskonen at Arctos.
